subject: small spider
title: A New Spider Builds a Spring Trap That Catapults Ants Into Its Web

scenes.text: A newly found spider doesn't chase ants. It launches them.
In the rainforest of northern Australia, a spider five millimeters long hangs a cone of silk below its web, pulled tight like a spring.
Building it takes up to four hours and as many as sixty lines of silk. Then the spider waits.
A green tree ant bites the cone. It snaps free, and the stored tension flings the ant upward, straight into the web.
The ant is hauled up more than a foot, at around 140 times the force of gravity.
Scientists revealed the ballista spider in 2026. It hunts one species of ant, and nothing else.

description:
A newly discovered Australian spider builds a spring-loaded trap that catapults ants into its web.
The ballista spider, an unnamed species in the genus Propostira, is about 5 mm long and lives in the rainforest of northern Queensland, above the foraging trails of green tree ants (Oecophylla smaragdina), the only prey it is known to take. It anchors a line to a leaf, pulls 15 to 60 tension lines down from its web into a cone, a job that can take four hours, and waits. When an ant bites the cone, it comes free of its anchor and the tension stored in the silk launches the ant more than 30 cm up into the web, with an acceleration of over 1,300 metres per second squared (about 140 g). Taxonomist Greg Anderson first saw the trap in 2023; the study with Ajay Narendra of Macquarie University was published in Current Biology in 2026. Whether the cone also lures ants with scent is still only a suspicion.
Would you have guessed a spider could build a catapult? Comment below.
first_comment: It was first spotted setting its trap in 2023 and still has no official species name. What would you call it?
